get.description:
Retrieve the authenticated user's collections using cursor-based pagination.
The Unsorted collection is always returned first, regardless of sort order, and is identified by its system_key ("unsorted").
Collections can be sorted by creation time (newest or oldest) or alphabetically by name. The default sort is "newest".
saved_items_count represents the number of saved items in a collection. Counts are exact up to 99; when saved_items_count_overflow is true, the count represents 99 or more.
Pass meta.cursor.next_cursor from the previous response to retrieve the next page. A null next_cursor indicates the final page.
Possible error codes:
- INVALID_COLLECTION_SORT
- INVALID_CURSOR
- VALIDATION_ERROR
- INVALID_AUTHORIZATION_HEADER
- INVALID_ACCESS_TOKEN
- ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRED
- INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR

parameters.description: Number of collections per page. Defaults to 20, capped at 50.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: Opaque cursor from meta.cursor.next_cursor of the previous page. Omit to start at the beginning.
parameters.name: cursor

200.description: One page of collections, with meta.cursor.next_cursor null when there is no next page

delete.description:
Delete one of the user's collections.
saved_items_action determines what happens to the saved items in the collection. "delete" deletes the saved items, while "move" moves them to the collection specified by target_collection_id before deleting the collection.
target_collection_id must be provided when saved_items_action is "move" and must be null when it is "delete". Unsorted can be used as a move destination.
The Unsorted collection cannot be deleted.
Possible error codes:
- BAD_REQUEST
- INVALID_COLLECTION_DELETE_ACTION
- INVALID_COLLECTION_DELETE_TARGET
- INVALID_AUTHORIZATION_HEADER
- INVALID_ACCESS_TOKEN
- ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRED
- COLLECTION_NOT_FOUND
- COLLECTION_DELETE_TARGET_NOT_FOUND
- UNSORTED_COLLECTION_PROTECTED
- COLLECTION_NOT_EMPTY
- INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR

Pass meta.cursor.next_cursor from the previous response to retrieve the next page. A null next_cursor indicates the final page.

get.description:
Search the authenticated user's saved items and collections.
Saved items are matched by title, domain, and URL. Collections are matched by name, including system collections.
Search supports partial matches and typo tolerance. Results are ranked by relevance, with recency used to break ties.
Results are limited and are not paginated.
Saved item results carry the item's collection, its enrichment_status and its optional note, so a client can tell where it lives, whether it has been read, and what the user wrote about it; each result is a subset of the item shape reported by GET /collections/{id}/saved-items. The note is reported but is not searchable.
Possible error codes:
- INVALID_SEARCH_QUERY
- INVALID_AUTHORIZATION_HEADER
- INVALID_ACCESS_TOKEN
- ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRED
- INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR

get.description:
Retrieve the authenticated user's profile, including linked authentication providers and whether the account has a password credential.
identities contains the authentication providers linked to the account. The array is always present and may be empty. Clients should support provider values they do not recognize.
email_snapshot and display_name_snapshot represent provider information captured when the identity was linked. They are historical values and are not refreshed, so they may differ from the user's current email and display name; nothing is fetched from the provider to reconcile them. Both fields may be null.
has_password_credential indicates whether the account has a password credential and can be used to determine which password settings options to display. The password update endpoint remains authoritative when applying changes.
Possible error codes:
- USER_NOT_FOUND
- INVALID_AUTHORIZATION_HEADER
- INVALID_ACCESS_TOKEN
- ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRED
- INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR

put.description:
Create a password for an account that does not have a password credential, or change the existing password.
Send new_password alone when creating a password. When changing an existing password, both new_password and current_password are required.
The operation is determined by the account's current password credential state. has_password_credential from GET /users/me is a UI hint; this endpoint remains authoritative.
Access tokens are stateless: revoking a session does not invalidate an access token that was already issued from it. Creating a password does not revoke existing sessions. Changing an existing password revokes all other active sessions while preserving the current session, but access tokens associated with revoked sessions may remain usable until they expire, which is at most 15 minutes.
The response message distinguishes between "password created successfully" and "password changed successfully".
Possible error codes:
- VALIDATION_ERROR
- BAD_REQUEST
- CURRENT_PASSWORD_REQUIRED
- UNEXPECTED_CURRENT_PASSWORD
- INVALID_AUTHORIZATION_HEADER
- INVALID_ACCESS_TOKEN
- ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRED
- CURRENT_PASSWORD_INVALID
- PASSWORD_CREDENTIAL_NOT_FOUND
- PASSWORD_CREDENTIAL_ALREADY_EXISTS
- PASSWORD_ALREADY_CHANGED
- USER_RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED
- USER_RATE_LIMIT_UNAVAILABLE
- PASSWORD_WORK_UNAVAILABLE
- INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR

has_more.description:
HasMore is computed from one row fetched beyond the requested limit, so it is
exact rather than inferred from a count. There is deliberately no total: a
cursor-paginated response does not know how many results exist overall.

next_cursor.description:
NextCursor is the token for the following page, or null on the final page and on
an empty result. It is null whenever has_more is false.

saved_items_action.description:
SavedItemsAction is what to do with the collection's saved items.

"delete" removes them along with the collection. "move" files them into
target_collection_id first, and then removes the collection. Both are
required: the request must say which, because the two are not variants of a
single outcome and one of them discards saved items.

target_collection_id.description:
TargetCollectionID is where the saved items go when SavedItemsAction is
"move".

It must be a collection id and must be null when SavedItemsAction is
"delete". Unsorted is a valid target and is named here by its id, like any
other collection; there is no separate mode or flag for it, and no fallback
to it. A target that does not exist is an error rather than a substitution.

saved_items_count.description:
SavedItemsCount is how many saved items the collection holds, capped at 99.

The two count fields together are the whole contract: a value from 0 to 99 is
exact, and 99 with saved_items_count_overflow true means "99 or more" rather
than "99". Splitting them is what lets a client render an exact badge up to 99
and a "99+" above it without ever comparing against a threshold this API
chose, and without the two states ever being confused for one another.

It counts the whole collection on every page. A count that described the page
rather than the collection would be a different number on each one, and a
badge that changes as the user scrolls is not a count of anything.

It is never null. A collection holding nothing reports 0, because a collection
holding nothing is an ordinary state in this product rather than an absence of
a count.

saved_items_count_overflow.description:
SavedItemsCountOverflow is true when the collection holds more saved items
than SavedItemsCount could show, which is to say more than 99.

It is a separate boolean rather than something inferred from the count so that
the threshold lives in one place on the server. A client comparing against its
own copy of 99 is a second source of truth for a product decision.

EnrichmentStatus is pending, completed or failed. Completed means the process
ran, not that every field above is populated, so completed with a null title is
normal.

LastEnrichedAt is null until an enrichment has succeeded at least once. A failed
attempt refreshes nothing, so it does not set this.

PriceAmount and PriceCurrency are the optional product price. price_amount is
a JSON string so a client never parses money through a float, and
price_currency is null when the source currency was unknown. Both are null when
no usable price was stored.

collection_intent.description:
CollectionIntent says which of the two operations the caller means.

"existing" selects a destination: a collection of either type that holds
the name is reused, and the move succeeds. "create" asks for a new
collection: a name that is already held by one of the user's collections
is refused with COLLECTION_NAME_ALREADY_EXISTS, and nothing is created or
moved.

There is no default. The same name means opposite things under the two
intents, so an absent value is an error rather than a guess. Like
CollectionName, this field carries no `validate` constraint because the
service owns the rule and answers with INVALID_COLLECTION_INTENT.

collection_name.description:
CollectionName is the display name of the collection to file the saved item
under. Any existing collection owned by the user is a valid destination,
including a system collection such as Unsorted or an automatically created
platform collection. Names are matched case-insensitively with surrounding
whitespace ignored, and the stored name is trimmed.

What happens when the name is already taken depends on CollectionIntent,
never on the name itself.

This field carries no `validate` constraint on purpose. The service owns
collection name rules and answers with the INVALID_COLLECTION_NAME code, so
a constraint here would pre-empt that and collapse both failure cases into a
generic VALIDATION_ERROR.

already_in_collection.description:
AlreadyInCollection is true when the saved item was already in the target
collection, in which case nothing was written. It is mutually exclusive with
CollectionCreated.

collection_created.description:
CollectionCreated is true only when this call created the collection. It is
false when an existing collection was reused.

enrichment_status.description:
EnrichmentStatus is pending, completed or failed. It is completed when the
enrichment process succeeded, which is not the same as every metadata field
being present.

last_enriched_at.description:
LastEnrichedAt is null until an enrichment has succeeded at least once. A
failed attempt does not set it, because nothing was refreshed.

price_amount.description:
PriceAmount and PriceCurrency are the optional product price stored by the
latest successful enrichment. price_amount is a JSON string so a client never
has to parse money through a floating point value; price_currency is null when
the source currency could not be normalized. Both are null when the page
exposed no usable price or when there was no title to anchor it to.

note.description:
Note is optional plain text the user wants to remember about this URL. It is
nullable and may span multiple lines, and leaving it out (or sending null)
preserves the existing save behavior exactly. A value containing only
whitespace is stored as NULL.

max=5000 is measured in runes by the validator, so a multilingual note is not
rejected for being long in bytes. The service applies the same bound again for
callers that reach it without this type.

enrichment_status.description:
EnrichmentStatus is the value the row was stored with, which on a fresh save is
always pending. Background enrichment has been queued by the time this returns
but has not run, so this response never reports completed.

note.description:
Note is the note that was actually stored with the save, or null when none was
submitted or when the submitted value contained only whitespace. Reporting it
here lets a caller confirm what was written without opening the item.
note.example: Read the section about database indexing later.

has_more.description:
HasMore is computed from one row fetched beyond the requested limit, so it is
exact rather than inferred from a count. There is deliberately no total: a
cursor-paginated response does not know how many results exist overall.

next_cursor.description:
NextCursor is the token for the following page, or null on the final page and on
an empty result. It is null whenever has_more is false.

collection_deletable.description:
CollectionDeletable is true when the collection is now empty and is not the
Unsorted collection.

collection_empty.description:
CollectionEmpty is true when the collection held no other saved item once
this one was gone.

collection.description:
Collection names the collection this item is filed in, as the same id and name
object GET /saved-items/{id} reports. It is inside the item rather than beside
the page because this listing spans every collection the caller owns: there is
no single collection for the response to name, so each row has to name its own.

It is read by the listing's own statement, so naming it costs nothing and a
client never has to make a request per row to learn where an item lives.
collection_id above always equals collection.id.

description.description:
Description and ImageURL are null until enrichment supplies them, and stay null
afterwards when a page exposed neither. Both are ordinary states rather than
defects, and neither is a reason to leave the item out of the history.

current_password.description:
CurrentPassword is required only when the account already holds a
credential. Supplying it for an account that holds none is refused with
UNEXPECTED_CURRENT_PASSWORD rather than ignored, because a caller told its
password was set while the password it sent was never checked would have no
way to learn that.

new_password.description: NewPassword is the password to store. It is never persisted as submitted.
